lesson_scope: Evaluating the discriminant b^2 - 4ac, classifying the nature and number of roots (D > 0, D = 0, D < 0), setting up conditions for equal roots (tangency / repeated root), distinct real roots, no real roots, and finding parameter ranges involving linear/quadratic inequalities in parameters.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating numerical discriminant and stating the number of real roots.

hints: Identify the coefficients of $2x^2 + 5x - 3 = 0$: $a = 2, b = 5, c = -3$.
Substitute into the discriminant formula: $D = b^2 - 4ac = 5^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 25 + 24 = 49$.
Since $D > 0$, the equation has $2$ distinct real roots.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the quadratic coefficients $a, b, c$:
$$a = 2, \quad b = 5, \quad c = -3$$

Substitute into the discriminant formula $D = b^2 - 4ac$:
$$D = 5^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 25 + 24 = 49$$

Classify the number of real roots based on the sign of $D$:
$$\text{Since } D = 49 > 0, \text{ there are } 2 \text{ distinct real roots.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that because $D > 0$, there are $2$ distinct real roots.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for parameter value given repeated root condition D = 0.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of setting D = 0 for a repeated root.

hints: For a quadratic equation to have a repeated root, the discriminant must be zero: $b^2 - 4ac = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
State the condition for a repeated (equal) root:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac = 0$$

Substitute $a = 1, b = -10, c = c$ into the condition:
$$(-10)^2 - 4(1)(c) = 0$$
$$100 - 4c = 0$$

Solve the linear equation for $c$:
$$4c = 100 \implies c = 25$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving linear parameter inequality for no real roots condition D < 0.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving D < 0 for no real roots.

hints: For an equation to have no real roots, the discriminant must be strictly negative: $b^2 - 4ac < 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the condition for no real roots:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac < 0$$

Solve the inequality for $k$:
$$4k > 36 \implies k > 9$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving parameter inequality for two distinct real roots with non-monic leading term.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving D > 0 with leading coefficient a > 1.

hints: For the equation to have two distinct real roots, require $b^2 - 4ac > 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the condition for two distinct real roots:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac > 0$$

Substitute $a = 3, b = -4, c = p$ into the inequality:
$$(-4)^2 - 4(3)(p) > 0$$
$$16 - 12p > 0$$

Solve for $p$ and reduce to simplest form:
$$12p < 16 \implies p < \dfrac{16}{12} \implies p < \dfrac{4}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving a quadratic inequality in parameter k for the real-roots condition D >= 0.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving quadratic inequality arising from D >= 0.

hints: For the equation to have real roots (distinct or repeated), the discriminant must be non-negative: $b^2 - 4ac \ge 0$.
Factorise $(k - 6)(k + 6) \ge 0$ to get the exterior intervals: $k \le -6$ or $k \ge 6$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the real-roots condition $D \ge 0$:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac \ge 0$$
$$k^2 - 4(1)(9) \ge 0$$
$$k^2 - 36 \ge 0$$

Factorise the quadratic difference of squares:
$$(k - 6)(k + 6) \ge 0$$
$$\text{Critical values: } k = -6 \quad \text{and} \quad k = 6$$

State the required solution set for $\ge 0$:
$$k \le -6 \quad \text{or} \quad k \ge 6$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: expanding, rearranging to standard form, and evaluating discriminant.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of expanding to ax^2+bx+c=0 before discriminant evaluation.

hints: Expand the left-hand side and subtract $2$ to write in standard form: $2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0$.
Since $D = 25 > 0$, the equation has $2$ distinct real roots.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and rearrange to standard quadratic form $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$:
$$x(2x - 3) = 2$$
$$2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0$$

Evaluate the discriminant:
$$D = (-3)^2 - 4(2)(-2) = 9 + 16 = 25$$

Classify the nature of the roots:
$$\text{Since } D = 25 > 0, \text{ the equation has } 2 \text{ distinct real roots.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that because $D > 0$, the equation has $2$ distinct real roots.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: calculating the discriminant and classifying roots as non-real.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires calculating discriminant to state the number of real roots.

hints: Since $D < 0$, the equation has no real roots ($0$ real roots).

walkthrough.text:
Identify the coefficients from $3x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0$:
$$a = 3, \quad b = -5, \quad c = 4$$

Calculate the discriminant $D = b^2 - 4ac$:
$$D = (-5)^2 - 4(3)(4) = 25 - 48 = -23$$

State the number of real roots based on the sign of $D$:
$$\text{Since } D = -23 < 0, \text{ the equation has } 0 \text{ real roots (no real roots).}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that because $D < 0$, the equation has $0$ real roots (no real roots).

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: solving b^2 - 4ac = 0 for parameter k giving two values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires setting discriminant to zero to find parameter values.

hints: Equal roots occur when the discriminant equals zero: $b^2 - 4ac = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the equal-roots condition:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac = 0$$

Solve for all real values of $k$:
$$k = \pm \sqrt{144} = \pm 12$$
$$k = 12 \quad \text{or} \quad k = -12$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: expressing discriminant algebraically and solving a quadratic inequality for distinct roots.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires algebraic formulation of discriminant in terms of parameter.

walkthrough.text:
Factor out $4$ from all terms:
$$D = 4(k^2 - 3k - 4)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires solving quadratic inequality for two distinct real roots.

hints: For two distinct real roots, require $D > 0 \implies 4(k^2 - 3k - 4) > 0$.
The critical values are $-1$ and $4$. For $> 0$, the solution is $k < -1$ or $k > 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the condition for distinct real roots:
$$4(k^2 - 3k - 4) > 0 \implies k^2 - 3k - 4 > 0$$
$$(k - 4)(k + 1) > 0$$

State the outside solution regions:
$$k < -1 \quad \text{or} \quad k > 4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding discriminant expression and solving for parameter range giving no real roots.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and simplify the algebraic expression:
$$D = 36 - 8(2p + 1) = 36 - 16p - 8 = 28 - 16p$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solves linear inequality for no real roots.

walkthrough.text:
Require the discriminant to be strictly negative for no real roots:
$$28 - 16p < 0$$

Solve the linear inequality for $p$:
$$16p > 28 \implies p > \dfrac{28}{16} \implies p > \dfrac{7}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: parameter in leading and constant terms, requiring non-zero domain handling for quadratic inequality.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forms quadratic inequality from D >= 0 with parameter in leading coefficient.

hints: For real roots, the discriminant must be non-negative: $b^2 - 4ac \ge 0$.

walkthrough.text:
State the condition on the discriminant for real roots:
$$D = b^2 - 4ac \ge 0$$

Substitute $a = k, b = 4, c = k$ into the formula:
$$4^2 - 4(k)(k) \ge 0$$
$$16 - 4k^2 \ge 0 \quad \left(\text{or } k^2 \le 4\right)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solves bounded parameter inequality excluding zero.

hints: Recall that $k$ is given as non-zero ($k \ne 0$) because it is the leading coefficient.
Exclude $0$ from the interval: $-2 \le k < 0$ or $0 < k \le 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the quadratic inequality $16 - 4k^2 \ge 0$:
$$4(4 - k^2) \ge 0 \implies (2 - k)(2 + k) \ge 0$$
$$-2 \le k \le 2$$

Apply the condition $k \ne 0$ to state the valid non-zero parameter set:
$$-2 \le k < 0 \quad \text{or} \quad 0 < k \le 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Excludes $k = 0$ to give $-2 \le k < 0$ or $0 < k \le 2$ (or $-2 \le k \le 2, k \ne 0$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: repeated root condition creating quadratic in m with exact surd solutions, and evaluating repeated root.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solves quadratic discriminant condition yielding exact surd parameters.

hints: Use quadratic formula or complete the square: $(m - 5)^2 - 25 + 17 = 0 \implies (m - 5)^2 = 8 \implies m = 5 \pm 2\sqrt{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set $D = 0$ for a repeated root:
$$(m - 3)^2 - 4(1)(m - 2) = 0$$

Expand and collect terms into standard quadratic form in $m$:
$$m^2 - 6m + 9 - 4m + 8 = 0$$
$$m^2 - 10m + 17 = 0$$

Solve for $m$ by completing the square or quadratic formula:
$$(m - 5)^2 - 25 + 17 = 0$$
$$(m - 5)^2 = 8$$
$$m = 5 \pm \sqrt{8} = 5 \pm 2\sqrt{2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Evaluates exact surd root corresponding to parametric solution.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $m = 5 + 2\sqrt{2}$ into the repeated root formula:
$$x = -\dfrac{(5 + 2\sqrt{2}) - 3}{2}$$

Simplify the exact expression:
$$x = -\dfrac{2 + 2\sqrt{2}}{2} = -(1 + \sqrt{2}) = -1 - \sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: algebraic expansion of complex discriminant, linear parameter inequality, and critical evaluation of leading coefficient breakdown.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proves linear discriminant reduction from quadratic binomial products.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the coefficients $a = 2k + 1, b = -4k, c = 2k - 3$ into $b^2 - 4ac$:
$$D = (-4k)^2 - 4(2k + 1)(2k - 3)$$

Expand each product carefully:
$$(-4k)^2 = 16k^2$$
$$(2k + 1)(2k - 3) = 4k^2 - 6k + 2k - 3 = 4k^2 - 4k - 3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solves no-real-roots condition and analyzes degenerate linear equation case.

hints: Note that $k = -\dfrac{1}{2} = -0.5 > -0.75$, which is outside the no-real-roots set.
When $k = -\dfrac{1}{2}$, the $x^2$ coefficient is $2(-\dfrac{1}{2}) + 1 = 0$, so the equation degenerates into a linear equation with one single root.

walkthrough.text:
Set $D < 0$ for no real roots:
$$16k + 12 < 0$$
$$16k < -12 \implies k < -\dfrac{12}{16} \implies k < -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Analyze the special value $k = -\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$\text{The leading coefficient is } a = 2k + 1 = 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 1 = 0$$

State what occurs when $k = -\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$\text{The equation becomes } 0x^2 - 4\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)x + \left(2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 3\right) = 0 \implies 2x - 4 = 0$$
$$\text{The quadratic degenerates into a linear equation with exactly one real solution } x = 2.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that at $k = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ the $x^2$ coefficient is 0, so the equation becomes linear with one solution.
